The Good Report according to

Matthew

Introduction

The (one) who wrote this document (LIT reading), was Matthew (MS Matiyu) who was also named Libi. He was one of the twelve (12) disciples of Jesus, and his father was_named Alpiyu. He was from_Galiliya but he worked at Kapirnaum as a collector of tax before becoming a disciple of Jesus. And it might be Jesus who changed his name of Libi when he became a disciple, and he was_named Matthew which means ‘the gift of God (MS Manama)’ in the Hibruwanon language.

The story of Matthew, (it) begins with the geneology of the ancestors of Jesus, his birth, baptism and the temptation of him, his preaching and teaching, and his healing of the sick (ones) in Galiliya. Finishing this, Matthew then tells about Jesus going to Hirusalim (MS Hirusalim), and what he did while he was there. He also told what happened in Jesus' final week in Hirusalim, the nailing of him to a cross, and his resurrection.

This reading tells that Jesus (MS Hisus), is the Christ who was promised by God to save the Hudiyus, and all of the non Hudiyus who believe and trust in him. And by_means of him, God fulfilled his promise to his people according to the Old Agreement.

This Good Report, (it) reveals that Jesus is the great/honored Teacher, and he has the right to explain the Law of God. Here in this document, there are five long teachings of Jesus that were_written by Matthew, especially the teaching of Jesus about the Reigning of God: (1) The preaching there at the mountain concerning the behavior of people, their duties and what they will_receive, and the end/destiny of people who become_members of the Reigning_place of God (Chapters 5–7); (2) the warnings to the twelve (12) apostles about their work (Chapter 10); (3) the examples/parables concerning the kingdom of God (Chapter 13); (4) the teaching about the meaning of becoming a disciple (Chapter 18); and (5) the teaching about the end of this time and about the Reigning of God which will_arrive. (Chapters 24–25).

2 Abraham is the father of Isaak, Isaak is the father of Hakub, and Hakub is the father of Huda and of his siblings. 3 Huda married Tamar and there were two children of theirs who were Piris and Sira. Piris is the father of Hisrun, and Hisrun is the father of Aram. 4 Aram is the father of Aminadab, Aminadab is the father of Nasun, and Nasun is the father of Salmun. 5 Salmun married Rahab and their child was Buas, and Buas married Rut and their child was Ubid, and Ubid is the father of Hisi, 6 and Hisi is the father of King Dabid.

King Dabid is the father of Solomon (MS Sulumun), and his mother was the former spouse of Uriyas.7 Solomon is the father of Rihubuam, Rihubuam is the father of Abyas, Abyas is the father of Asa, 8 and Asa is the father of Hihusapat, Hihusapat is the father of Huram, Huram is the father of Usiyas. 9 Usiyas is the father of Hutam, Hutam is the father of Ahas, Ahas is the father of Isikiyas. 10 Isikiyas is the father of Manasis, Manasis is the father of Amun, and Amun is the father of Husiyas. 11 [xr]Husiyas is the father of Hikuniyas and his siblings. At that time, the (ones) from_Israil were_taken to Babilunya in_order to be enslaved.

12 After the (ones) from_Israil were_taken by the (ones) from_Babilunya, Hikuniyas fathered Salatiil, and Salatiil is the father of Surubabil, 13 Surubabil is the father of Abyud, Abyud is the father of Ilyakim, Ilyakim is the father of Asur, 14 Asur is the father of Saduk, and Saduk is the father of Akim, Akim is the father of Ilyud. 15 Ilyud is the father of Ilisar, Ilisar is the father of Matan, Matan is the father of Hakub. 16 Hakub is the father of Husi, who is the spouse of Mary (MS Mariya) the mother of Jesus who is named Christ.

17 Therefore there are fourteen (14) descendants/generations from Abraham until Dabid, and also fourteen (14) descendants/generations from Dabid until the time that the (ones) from_Israil were_taken to Babilunya, and there were yet also fourteen (14) descendants/generations from (when) the (ones) from_Israil were_taken until the Christ[fn] was_born.

And he will_return accompanied by the clouds in the sky.”

65 [xr]At that, the Great/Prominent Sacrificer tore his clothing and said, “He has mocked God! So why will we(incl) still need to get witnesses when you(pl) have heard his mocking? 66 Now_then, what do you(pl) think?”

And they answered, “He's worthy of being killed!”

67 [xr]Afterwards, they spat on his face, and they beaten (LIT strike_with_fists) him and he was slapped by others 68 who said, “So then Christ, guess(sg) who it was who hurt you(sg)!”

The denying of Pidru about Jesus

(Mar 14:66‑72; Luk 22:56‑62; Jhn 18:15‑18, 25‑27)

69 Meanwhile Pidru was sitting in the yard. And there_was a female servant of the Great/Prominent Sacrificer who approached him and said, “Hey, it seems like you(sg) (are) a companion of Jesus from Galiliya?”

70 But Pidru denied (it) there in front of all the people and said, “I don't know what you(sg) are_talking_about.” 71 Then, he went to the fence boundary and there_was again a different female servant who saw him, and said to the people, “Hey, this person is a companion of Jesus from Nasarit.”

72 And Pidru denied it again and said, “Truly by oath, I don't know that person!”

73 Before long, those standing there approached Pidru and said, “It is indeed true that you(sg) (are) a companion of them because you(sg) are recognized even by your(sg) speaking.”

74 Then, Pidru really swore saying, “I swear by myself, I really don't know that person even if I will_die!” And immediately the chicken crowed 75 and Pidru remembered what Jesus had said to him, “Before the chicken crows, you(sg) will_deny me three times.” And Pidru exited and cried intensely.

The taking of Jesus to Pilate (MS Pilatu)

(Mar 15:1; Luk 23:1‑2; Jhn 18:28‑32)

271 When morning came, the leaders of the sacrificers and the elders of the Hudiyus planned how Jesus was to_be_killed. 2 And they bound Jesus and then took (him) to Governor Pilate, and they gave him (over) to him.

The death of Judas

(Act 1:18‑19)

3 [xr]When Judas the betrayer saw their judgment to cause_ Jesus _to_be_killed, he regretted (it) and he returned the thirty (30) pieces of money to the leaders of the sacrificers and to the elders of the Hudiyus. 4 He said, “I've sinned by betraying a person without sin.”

And they answered, “What's our(excl) responsibility for that? That's your(sg) problem!”

5 And Judas tossed the money into the temple and he left. Then, (he) went and committed_suicide by hanging (himself).

6 The leaders of the sacrificers picked up the money and said, “This money, is payment for the life of a person, and it's against our(incl) law to put this in the money container here in the temple.” 7 Therefore they agreed that they would use_ the money _to_buy the field of the maker of clay_pot(s) to make (it) a cemetery of foreigners. 8 And so, even now that is called, “Land that was Paid for with Blood.”

9 [xr]Therefore what the prophet Hirimiyas said was fulfilled, “They took the thirty (30) pieces of money, the amount that was agreed_on by the descendants of Israil[fn] as payment for him. 10 And they used the money and they bought the field of the maker of clay_pot(s), according to the command of God to me.”

The repeatedly_questioning of Jesus by Pilate

(Mar 15:2‑5; Luk 23:3‑5; Jhn 18:33‑38)

11 And Jesus was in front of Governor Pilate, and he was_questioned by Pilate who said, “Are you(sg) really the king of the Hudiyus?”

Jesus answered, “You(sg) indeed said (it).”12 But he didn't answer the accusations of the leaders of the sacrificer(s) and of the elders of the Hudiyus.

13 Therefore Pilate said to him, “Don't you(sg) hear their many accusations to you(sg)?”

14 But Jesus really didn't answer even one of their accusations, therefore the Governor was greatly amazed.

The sentencing of Jesus death

(Mar 15:6‑15; Luk 23:13‑25; Jhn 18:39–19:16)

15 It was Pilate's custom each Feast of the Passing_by of the Angel, that he released a prisoner that the people wanted. 16 At that time, there_was one famous prisoner called Barabas.[fn] 17 When the many people were gathered, they were asked by Pilate, “Who do you(pl) want me to release? Barabas or Jesus who is called the Christ?” 18 Because Pilate knew that they were just envious of Jesus, so_that's why they had arrested Jesus and given (him) to him.

19 While Pilate was sitting on the judging seat, his spouse sent him a message that said, “Don't(sg) meddle with that righteous person, because I was troubled (LIT anxious) by my dream about him yesterday.”

20 But the leaders of the sacrificers and the elders of the Hudiyus persuaded the people that they should request that Barabas be released, and for Jesus to be_killed. 21 And Pilate asked the people again, “Who of the two here do you(pl) want me to release?”

They answered, “Barabas!”

22 And Pilate said to them, “If it's like that, what should I do to Jesus who is called the Christ?”

They all answered saying, “Nail(sg) him to a cross!”

23 And Pilate asked them, “Why, what crime (LIT bad) has he done?”

But they just yelled all_the_more saying, “Nail(sg) him to a cross!”

24 [xr]When Pilate saw that there_was_nothing more he could do but rather the people were stirred_up, he got water and washed_(hands) there in front of the people and said, “I am not involved in the death of this person! That's your(pl) responsibility!”

25 And all the people answered, “We(excl) along_with our(excl) children will_answer for the death of that person.”

26 Afterwards, Pilate caused_ Barabas _to_be_released, and he caused_ Jesus _to_be_beaten and he gave him to the soldiers in_order to_be_nailed to a cross.

The insulting of Jesus by the soldiers

(Mar 15:16‑20; Jhn 19:2‑3)

27 Afterwards, Jesus was_taken by the soldiers to the palace of the governor, and they gathered_together all their fellow soldiers. 28 They stripped him and they dressed (him) in a scarlet (LIT bright_red) garment. 29 And they made a thorn crown and they crowned Jesus. And they caused_ him _to_hold_a_staff in his right hand and they kneeled in front of him and blasphemed him and said, “May the king of the Hudiyus be honored/famous!” 30 Afterwards, they spat on Jesus and took the staff and they beat his head. 31 When they had_finished blaspheming him, they took off what they had put on him and dressed him back with his former clothes. Then, they took him outside to nail to a cross.

The nailing of Jesus to a cross

(Mar 15:21‑32; Luk 23:26‑43; Jhn 19:17‑27)

32 When they had_gone_out, they met a (person) from Sirini called Simun, and they persuaded/forced him to carry_on_(his)_shoulder the cross of Jesus. 33 Then, they arrived at the place called Gulguta (Place of the Skull is the meaning of this), 34 [xr]and they gave Jesus wine mixed with (something) bitter to drink, but when he tasted it, he didn't drink (it).

35 [xr]Then, they nailed Jesus to a cross, and they divided his clothes by mean of drawing_lots. 36 When that was_finished, they sat and they watched_over him. 37 And they put a signboard above the head of Jesus that was_written with the charge about him that said, “This is Jesus the king of the Hudiyus.” 38 There were two thieves that they crucified with him. One was on his right and the other on his left.

39 [xr]And those who passed there, shook_their_heads_from_side_to_side insulting Jesus 40 [xr]saying, “Oh, you(sg) (surprise) are really the one would demolish the temple and rebuild it within just three days! If you(sg) (are) the Child of God, save yourself and come down from the cross.”

41 Also like that were the leaders of the sacrificer(s), the teachers of the Law of God, and the elders of the Hudiyus who jeered at him like this, 42 “He saved others, but he can't save himself! They_say he is the king of Israil! If he comes down from the cross now, we(incl) will_believe and trust (in) him. 43 [xr]He (hearsay) trusted God, so God can be the one to rescue him if he wants, because he said, ‘I (am) the child of God.’ ”

44 And Jesus' companions on the cross(es) also jeered at him.

The death of Jesus

(Mar 15:33‑41; Luk 23:44‑49; Jhn 19:28‑30)

45 At noon, the entire nation became dark until three o'clock in the afternoon.[fn] 46 [xr]At three o'clock in the afternoon,[fn] Jesus shouted loudly like_this, “Ili, Ili, lima sabaktani?” For us(incl) it's, “God, God, why am I deserted by you(sg)?”

47 When some people standing there heard that, they said, “He is calling Ilyas!” 48 [xr]And immediately one of them ran to get something like foam_mattress and soaked it in sour wine and tied it to a stick in_order_to cause_ Jesus _to_suck (it).

49 But the others said, “Just let it be (idiom LIT stay(sg) here), we(incl) will_see if Ilyas comes_here to save him.”

50 Then, Jesus shouted loudly again, and then he stopped_breathing.

51 [xr]Also at just that time, the curtain in the temple was torn from the top to the bottom. And there_was an earthquake and the rockfaces were split, 52 and the tombs were_opened, and the dead people of God came_alive, 53 and they exited out of their tombs. When Jesus came alive, they went to the holy city of Hirusalim and showed themselves to the people.

54 The captain of the soldiers and his companions that were watching Jesus, were_ very _afraid when the earth_shook and when they saw the wonders that happened at the death of Jesus and they said, “It's indeed true that that person was the Child of God!”

55 [xr]And there were also many women that were watching from some distance. They were the ones who followed and looked_after Jesus before from Galiliya still. 56 There was Mariya Magdalina, Mariya the mother of James and Husi, and the mother of the children of Sibidiyu.

The wrapping_and_storing of Jesus' (body)

(Mar 15:42‑47; Luk 23:50‑56; Jhn 19:38‑42)

57 When it became_dark, a rich (man) from_Arimatiya called Husi arrived and he was also a disciple of Jesus. 58 He went to Pilate and he requested the body of Jesus. And Pilate commanded that this be given to him. 59 And Husi took the body of Jesus and wrapped this in clean cloth, 60 and he wrapped_the_body_and_stored in the rock/cliff that was still newly hewn_out. And he rolled a big stone/rock to shut the entrance of the burial_storage_place, and then, he left. 61 And Mariya Magdalina and someone_with_the_same_name, sat in front of the burial_storage_place.

The watching_over of the burial_storage_place

62 The next day, the Day of Resting, the leaders of the sacrificers and the Pharisees went to Pilate 63 [xr]and said, “Master, we(excl) remember that cheater said before his death that he would come_alive on the third day. 64 Therefore you(sg) cause_ the burial_storage_place _to_be_watched for three days so_that his body isn't stolen by his disciples and then, they will_tell the people that he is alive. And this final cheating, (it) will_become worse than the first.”

65 And Pilate said to them, “Take(pl) (some) soldiers and go. Now_then, cause_ the burial_storage_place _to_be_watched_over by them carefully.”

66 Therefore they went and secured the burial_storage_place by_means of putting a sign on the closing stone/rock. And then, they caused_(it)_to_be_watched_over.

The coming_alive of Jesus

(Mar 16:1‑10; Luk 24:1‑12; Jhn 20:1‑10)

281 When the Day of Resting had passed, when it was still early_morning on the day of Sunday, Mariya Magdalina visited the burial_storage_place along_with her namesake Mariya. 2 And suddenly a strong earthquake came, because there_was an angel of the Lord God that descended from heaven/sky. And he went to the burial_storage_place and rolled the stone/rock that covered it, and he sat on (it). 3 His face was like a flash of lightning and his clothing was extremely white. 4 And those guards, shook with their fright and they fainted (LIT their souls left them).

5 And the angel said to the women, “Don't(pl) be_afraid! I know that you(pl) are looking for Jesus who was nailed on a cross. 6 He's no_longer here because he came_alive as per what he said. So come_here(pl), look(pl) at his laying_place. 7 And go(pl) straight_away to his disciples and tell(pl) them that he has come_alive. He preceded you(pl) to Galiliya and you(pl) will_see him there. Don't forget(pl) what_ I _told you(pl).”

8 There they left the burial_storage_place straight_away and were_afraid and happy also, and they ran to tell his disciples.

9 While they were still on the road, suddenly Jesus met them and said, “Hello.” And they approached Jesus and touched his feet and they worshiped him. 10 Then, Jesus said to them, “Don't(pl) be_afraid! Go(pl) and tell my siblings to go to Galiliya and they will_see me there.”

The story of the guards

11 While the women were_ still _walking, some of the burial_storage_place guards went to the city and told to the leaders of the sacrificers everything that had happened. 12 And the leaders of the sacrificers gathered along_with the elders, and they planned that the soldiers would_be_given lots of money. 13 They said to the soldiers, “Tell(pl) the people that his disciples went there at night and took the body while you(pl) were sleeping. 14 And if/when this is heard by the governor, we(excl) will_take_responsibility to explain to him so_that you(pl) will_have_no reason to be worried.”

15 Therefore they took the money and they obeyed what they were_told_to_do. Even now, that very story is spread everywhere by the Hudiyus.

The revealing of Jesus to his disciples

(Mar 16:14‑18; Luk 24:36‑49; Jhn 20:19‑23; Act 1:6‑8)

16 [xr]And those eleven (11) disciples of his, went to Galiliya to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go. 17 When they saw him, they worshiped him but some of them doubted. 18 And Jesus approached them and said, “All of the authority in heaven/sky and here on top of the earth has been_given to me. 19 [xr]Therefore go_there(pl) to the people in all places and make them my disciples. Baptize(pl) them in the name of the Father, the Child, and the Spirit of God. 20 Teach(pl) them to obey all I have commanded you(pl). And remember that I will always indeed accompany you(pl), until the end of time.”
